meta.caveat: Architecture-first seed for UI; not claimed ladder-optimal. Scores describe species/form tendencies across plausible Champions doubles architectures rather than one exact set. Regulation M-C allows one Mega Evolution per battle and forbids duplicate held items. ([Champions News][1])
meta.scale: All numeric scores are integers 0–5 unless noted. 0 = absent, 3 = solid, 5 = elite for Champions doubles architectures.

metricDefs.label: Engine Participation Count
metricDefs.meaning: How many distinct win engines / infrastructure loops this species can meaningfully participate in across common Champions doubles architectures, rather than within only one team.

metricDefs.label: Engine Exclusivity Tax
metricDefs.meaning: How often teammates must become dedicated servants for this species to function. High tax means packages collapse around it; low tax means many packages can support it lightly.

metricDefs.label: Bridge Quality
metricDefs.meaning: How effectively this species participates in separate modules without forcing either module to compromise.

metricDefs.label: Create Fan-Out
metricDefs.meaning: How many strategically distinct teammate roles can consume what this species creates.

metricDefs.label: Convert Fan-Out
metricDefs.meaning: How many distinct infrastructure forms this species can convert into progress, such as weather, Tailwind, Fake Out turns, terrain, Intimidate turns, screens, Trick Room, redirection, or free setup turns.

metricDefs.label: MAG
metricDefs.meaning: Marginal Architecture Gain — how much genuinely new strategic territory this species tends to open on Champions doubles sixes at species baseline rather than in one specific six.

metricDefs.label: Module Elasticity Support
metricDefs.meaning: As a root or key module, how many strategically different packages it can support without rebuilding the six.

metricDefs.label: Engine-Converter Continuity
metricDefs.meaning: How effectively this species can create a favorable resource or state and later personally convert that same state into damage, control, scaling, or a win condition instead of requiring another dedicated converter.

teamContextRules.cMagHint: Start with species-baseline MAG, then inspect the five teammates for duplicated territory. Raise C-MAG when the candidate adds a genuinely new engine, failure condition, speed state, damage axis, counterplay inversion, Mega package, or conversion route that existing teammates can also exploit. Lower C-MAG when it merely strengthens an already-saturated route without creating a meaningfully different package or failure state.
teamContextRules.exclusivityGivenSix: Lower Engine Exclusivity Tax when the other five already provide the infrastructure this species wants while remaining useful in unrelated packages. Lower it further when the species can function autonomously after consuming that infrastructure. Raise it when several teammates must change moves, items, Mega choice, positioning, speed profiles, or normal roles primarily to enable this species. Shared infrastructure with multiple consumers lowers tax; dedicated servants raise it.
teamContextRules.saturation: Adding another member of the same archetype lowers C-MAG when both create or consume the same resources, compete for the same setup or Mega turn, fail to the same counterplay, or improve the same packages without opening new ones. Functional redundancy remains valuable when the new species converts shared infrastructure differently, creates another speed or damage state, supplies a different endgame, or turns the first route's counterplay into progress for a second route.

profiles.name: Mega Garchomp Z
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: It is easy to misclassify through old physical-Garchomp assumptions; its architectural value is closer to a fast special coverage converter.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite Fan-In from generic tempo resources with low servant tax and unusually broad coverage conversion.
antiPatterns: Building Sand around it automatically
Treating it as interchangeable with standard Mega Garchomp
profiles.caveat: Mega Garchomp Z is newly legal in M-C, so exact package norms are still developing. ([Champions News][1])

profiles.name: Gardevoir
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its biggest architectural strength is not Fairy damage but the ability to bridge fast and slow packages through Trick Room without becoming passive.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Can personally spend the Trick Room it creates and still convert ordinary tempo resources.
antiPatterns: Treating Gardevoir as only a Fairy attacker

profiles.name: Mega Gardevoir
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: A premier example of engine-converter continuity: it can establish the alternate speed state and immediately become one of that state's strongest consumers.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite on both create and convert axes; particularly valuable in teams where Trick Room is one branch rather than the whole identity.
antiPatterns: Building a hard Trick Room six when Mega Gardevoir already supports mixed-speed architecture

profiles.name: Mega Gengar
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its value is not just speed and damage; fast disruption can manufacture the same free turns that Gengar itself later converts.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Excellent ECC and low exclusivity make it unusually efficient for a disruptive Mega.
antiPatterns: Using Mega Gengar as a generic fast attacker and ignoring its control leverage
profiles.caveat: Current M-C Mega results support Mega Gengar as one of the stronger-performing Mega options. ([Pokémon Zone - Pokémon TCG Pocket][2])

profiles.name: Gholdengo
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: One of the format's purest high-Fan-In converters: almost every form of tempo can become either Nasty Plot or immediate spread pressure.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Extremely low exclusivity because its preferred infrastructure is generic and usually benefits other teammates too.
antiPatterns: Greeding Nasty Plot when immediate Make It Rain already converts the board

profiles.name: Mega Glalie
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its damage can convert common speed and tempo resources, but the Mega slot often has to justify relatively limited outward infrastructure.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate Fan-In, modest bridge value.
antiPatterns: Using several support slots merely to keep Glalie attacking

profiles.name: Mega Glimmora
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Glimmora is valuable when chip creation and immediate special offense coexist rather than when either is treated as its only job.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good ECC because chip it helps establish can later become its own cleanup resource.
antiPatterns: Building passive hazard-style pressure without immediate doubles conversion
profiles.caveat: Mega Glimmora is currently among the more successful M-C Mega options, but exact architecture depends heavily on set. ([Pokémon Zone - Pokémon TCG Pocket][2])

profiles.name: Golisopod
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its strongest architecture is usually as one of several slow or priority converters rather than a sole centerpiece.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Broad inward graph across Trick Room, Rain, Fake Out, and chip.
antiPatterns: Making every support slot serve Golisopod setup

profiles.name: Mega Golisopod
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Golisopod improves dramatically when treated as one of several consumers of shared slow-game infrastructure rather than as a team that must be served.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite conversion Fan-In; Fake Out, Trick Room, Rain, Intimidate, and Armor Tail-style protection can all become Golisopod progress.
antiPatterns: Using Trick Room only for Golisopod
Trying to win through neutral chip instead of decisive setup conversion
profiles.caveat: Mega Golisopod is newly legal in M-C and has Tough Claws. ([Champions News][1])

profiles.name: Mega Golurk
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its coverage can be excellent under Trick Room, but speed-state dependence creates a substantial exclusivity tax.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Good slow-board converter, weak outward graph.
antiPatterns: Building hard Trick Room when only Golurk truly needs it

profiles.name: Mega Greninja
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Low support tax and broad coverage make it a strong example of a converter that can enter many packages without owning them.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In from weather, speed, tempo, and simple chip.
antiPatterns: Building excessive support for a Mega that should function with light infrastructure

profiles.name: Grimmsnarl
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: An elite outward-graph species: almost any scaler can spend what Grimmsnarl creates.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Low personal conversion is acceptable because the support has extreme Fan-Out and near-zero exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Pairing screens with a six that has no durable or setup converters

profiles.name: Gyarados
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Gyarados is more than a Dragon Dance consumer because Intimidate lets it create setup access for itself and partners.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Strong ECC with excellent generic Fan-In.
antiPatterns: Using Intimidate only defensively instead of converting the reduced-pressure turn

profiles.name: Mega Gyarados
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Pre-Mega Intimidate gives the Mega form unusually strong phase-transition value rather than making the Mega merely a stat upgrade.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High ECC: it can create a safer board before Mega and then become the main converter.
antiPatterns: Mega evolving immediately when pre-Mega Intimidate or typing still has work to do

profiles.name: Hawlucha
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: A strong inward-conversion species whose best sets can reduce exclusivity by self-triggering Unburden.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Self-activation raises ECC substantially relative to terrain-only Hawlucha.
antiPatterns: Using a dedicated terrain setter only to activate Hawlucha

profiles.name: Mega Hawlucha
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Hawlucha's main architecture is conversion rather than support; it needs little more than generic tempo if its base speed already fits the matchup.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Very high Fan-In but less engine creation than base Unburden identities.
antiPatterns: Over-supporting a Mega whose job should be immediate conversion

profiles.name: Mega Heracross
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: It converts many resources brilliantly, but most arrows point inward and teammates often pay heavily to manufacture its attacking turns.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Textbook high-Fan-In, high-exclusivity converter.
antiPatterns: Turning four teammates into dedicated speed, redirection, and survival support

profiles.name: Mega Houndoom
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Sun improves it substantially, but it can still convert generic speed and tempo without making the whole team Sun-dependent.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High convert Fan-Out with moderate outward graph.
antiPatterns: Building a full Sun composition solely to enable Houndoom

profiles.name: Incineroar
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: One of the format's purest engine hubs because the same Intimidate, Fake Out, and pivot package can feed almost any converter.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Personal damage is secondary, but Incineroar has strong ECC because it can repeatedly convert its own disruption into better positioning.
antiPatterns: Cycling Incineroar without a specific resource purchase

profiles.name: Indeedee Female
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Indeedee-F creates multiple distinct resources at once, so the same slot can support terrain offense, Seed activation, Trick Room, and generic setup.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate personal Fan-In, but elite create Fan-Out makes low ECC irrelevant.
antiPatterns: Using Psychic Terrain when only one teammate benefits from it

profiles.name: Indeedee Male
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Male Indeedee sacrifices redirection but gains more direct engine-converter continuity through offensive and speed-state sets.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Higher personal conversion than Indeedee-F while preserving much of the same terrain Fan-Out.
antiPatterns: Copying Indeedee-F's job description instead of exploiting Male Indeedee's offensive and speed-state flexibility

profiles.name: Mega Kangaskhan
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Kangaskhan is unusual because one of its primary infrastructure moves, Fake Out, shares a slot with a fully autonomous physical converter.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Excellent ECC and low servant tax.
antiPatterns: Treating Mega Kangaskhan as only a Fake Out support piece

profiles.name: Kingambit
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Kingambit is one of the best failure-inversion pieces because normal physical counterplay can become its own offensive infrastructure.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite Fan-In with almost no servant tax; works in fast teams, slow teams, or as a self-contained endgame.
antiPatterns: Saving Kingambit only for Trick Room packages

profiles.name: Kommo-o
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Kommo-o can convert many common setup resources, but its most explosive routes still tempt teams into over-supporting one scaler.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In, moderate-to-high exclusivity depending whether immediate attacks remain credible.
antiPatterns: Making every package depend on one successful setup sequence

profiles.name: Mega Lopunny
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Lopunny combines premium tempo creation with immediate high-speed conversion, giving it exceptional ECC.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Very low exclusivity because Fake Out itself is useful to almost every package while Lopunny needs little dedicated support.
antiPatterns: Using Fake Out without defining what the partner purchases with the free action

profiles.name: Lucario
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Lucario's flexibility comes from consuming many generic resources without demanding a specific dedicated engine.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In with low support tax.
antiPatterns: Overcommitting to setup when immediate Fighting or Steel pressure is enough

profiles.name: Mega Lucario
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its key architecture is not support creation but how efficiently generic tempo becomes lethal Fighting or Steel conversion.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In and low servant tax.
antiPatterns: Building a narrow support shell around a Mega that should convert immediately

profiles.name: Mega Lucario Z
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: The Z form deserves independent evaluation because its conversion profile and Mega preview implications differ from standard Mega Lucario.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Strong generic infrastructure consumer with low exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Assuming standard Mega Lucario package logic transfers unchanged
profiles.caveat: Mega Lucario Z is newly legal under M-C; exact tournament role remains in active development. ([Champions News][1])

profiles.name: Mega Malamar
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Malamar's strongest architecture emerges when opponent stat control becomes fuel instead of merely something it ignores.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In from opponent actions as well as friendly infrastructure.
antiPatterns: Building around Malamar without opponents having meaningful stat-control incentives

profiles.name: Mega Manectric
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Manectric's architecture is Salamence-like in miniature: it can create reduced-pressure states, pivot, and personally convert speed into damage.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Excellent ECC and almost no servant tax.
antiPatterns: Using Intimidate cycles without converters that exploit the reduced pressure

profiles.name: Mawile
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Even without Mega evolving, Mawile can bridge physical control and slow offense through Intimidate plus typing.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate Fan-In with useful ECC.
antiPatterns: Treating base Mawile as only a waiting room for Mega evolution

profiles.name: Mega Mawile
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: The important architecture is the phase transition from pre-Mega Intimidate utility into one of the strongest slow physical converters.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High ECC and strong Fan-In, especially when Trick Room already benefits other teammates.
antiPatterns: Mega evolving before pre-Mega Intimidate has purchased its value

profiles.name: Mega Medicham
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: The conversion ceiling is high, but Medicham itself contributes relatively little infrastructure and often needs careful turn manufacturing.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In, moderate exclusivity.
antiPatterns: Stacking multiple dedicated protection tools just to get Medicham attacks

profiles.name: Meganium
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Meganium is primarily an outward resource creator; its value depends on several teammates being able to convert durability.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Low personal Fan-In, but low exclusivity when screens and sustain have broad team value.
antiPatterns: Pairing defensive support with teammates that do not scale or exploit extra turns

profiles.name: Mega Meganium
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Mega Meganium can avoid the pure-support Mega trap if defensive infrastructure transitions into its own durable board presence.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Much better ECC than base Meganium while retaining strong outward Fan-Out.
antiPatterns: Using the Mega slot for pure defense without a conversion plan

profiles.name: Mega Meowstic Female
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Female Meowstic should be evaluated more as a high-Fan-In offensive/control node than as a generic support Psychic.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Broad conversion surface area with moderate create-web.
antiPatterns: Assigning Male Meowstic-style support expectations to the female form
profiles.caveat: Form-specific Mega roles remain less tournament-established than top M-C Megas.

profiles.name: Mega Meowstic Male
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Male Meowstic's architecture is primarily outward; it becomes worthwhile when several teammates can spend its priority support rather than one carry.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Moderate personal conversion but elite support Fan-Out.
antiPatterns: Using the Mega slot for support that only one teammate consumes
profiles.caveat: Form-specific Mega roles remain less tournament-established than top M-C Megas.

profiles.name: Metagross
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Metagross is architecturally strong because it can live in both fast and slow packages without demanding either.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Broad Fan-In and low support tax.
antiPatterns: Treating Metagross as requiring one fixed speed mode

profiles.name: Mega Metagross
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Its exceptional stat profile matters architecturally because almost any generic speed or defensive infrastructure becomes immediate conversion.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Very high Fan-In with low exclusivity and strong package flexibility.
antiPatterns: Over-supporting a Mega that is already highly autonomous

profiles.name: Milotic
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Milotic is both an opponent-funded engine and an autonomous control scaler, making it unusually resistant to single-route disruption.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite ECC: opponent stat control, friendly Fake Out, Intimidate support, and its own Coil all feed future conversion.
antiPatterns: Treating Milotic only as anti-Intimidate coverage
Using Hypnosis before creating a reliable accuracy or board context

profiles.name: Oranguru
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Oranguru becomes architecturally excellent when multiple partners can spend Trick Room and Instruct rather than one dedicated nuke.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Low personal conversion; its value is very high outward Fan-Out.
antiPatterns: Building around one Instruct target
Using Trick Room when only one teammate becomes faster

profiles.name: Passimian
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Passimian is valuable when Intimidate deterrence itself protects other physical attackers, not just when Passimian gets boosted.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Low servant tax and strong conversion of opponent counterplay.
antiPatterns: Using Passimian on teams where opponents have little reason to Intimidate

profiles.name: Pelipper
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Pelipper is an elite engine hub because Rain, Tailwind, and defensive utility can all feed different packages while Pelipper still converts Rain itself.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: Elite ECC and Fan-Out with almost no exclusivity when multiple partners independently use Rain.
antiPatterns: Building Rain so narrowly that removing weather disables every converter

profiles.name: Mega Pidgeot
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Pidgeot's strongest architecture is engine-converter continuity: it can establish Tailwind and then personally exploit the speed state.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High ECC with low support tax, though less defensive utility than Salamence or Staraptor.
antiPatterns: Using Tailwind without allowing Pidgeot itself to remain an active converter

profiles.name: Mega Pinsir
profiles.whyUnderOrOverRated: Pinsir converts generic speed and tempo well but contributes less infrastructure than premium bridge Megas.
profiles.conversionMonsterNote: High Fan-In, moderate exclusivity, strongest when its support also serves another scaler.
antiPatterns: Making Tailwind, redirection, and setup support all exist only for Pinsir
